column1: # Obligation citations — goal 0009a (the native oracle, re-scoped), the machine-checked half of the
# increment's acceptance surface (docs/goals/0009a-native-oracle.md).
# **What a row here is, exactly.** This increment makes no Go change (its Bounds), so it adds no Go
# test; docs/conventions.md holds a citations row to be one *gate-runnable Go test* in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers. Every row below therefore names one **surviving oracle rule** — the
# rule ids are `scripts/codex-native-check.py`'s `ORACLE_RULES` keys — and the existing Go test that
# already pins the same claim about this tree's own bytes: the sentence the rule restates, true of the
# writer (and of the committed fixtures) today and re-derived by this step when the gate runs. Where
# the rule states more than one clause, the `artifact` cell names the clause the cited test pins, and
# the row is no claim of conjunct-level coverage of the whole sentence. A row makes no claim that a Go
# test runs the oracle.
# The oracle's own firing is re-derived by the required `selftest` step instead:
# `scripts/tests/test_codex_native_check.py`'s `CodexArtifactOracle` drives the shipped rule table and
# its mutation corpus — every rule has at least one committed fixture whose mutation turns that rule
# red (beside exactly the other rules its bytes are known to break, the pair's `also_cited`), every arm
# (positive PASS, negative FAIL citing those, `--disable-rule` PASS or still FAIL citing exactly the
# other rules) is read through the shipped command's own `--validate`/`--receipt`/`--disable-rule` path,
# and the two tables are asserted in bijection from both ends — the increment's D1. The fixtures are
# `scripts/tests/testdata/codex-oracle/` (the frozen artifact and the receipt that names its bytes).
# Deliberately not covered, with the reason (form-based: a row is one Go test in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers, so a rule whose gate re-derivation is a python case the required
# `selftest` step runs, or a native harness run, cannot hold one):
#   oracle.utf8, oracle.whole-lines — no Go test pins the writer's document as UTF-8 text, as opening
#         with no byte-order mark, or as a sequence of line-feed-terminated lines: the writer emits
#         through `json.Encoder` (whose newline is the record terminator: internal/ccc/codex_target.go)
#         and every case that reads an installed document splits it on line feeds, but none asserts the
#         artifact's own final byte or its encoding. Their re-derivation is the same `selftest` case's
#         corpus — the mutations `a byte that is not UTF-8`, `a byte-order mark` and `a record left
#         unterminated`, each turning its own rule red through the shipped command — beside the
#         surviving corpus cases:
#         `test_the_frozen_artifact_validates` (D4's verify case: the artifact's size, whole-file digest
#         and per-line anchors are the committed receipt's own statements),
#         `test_a_mutated_byte_breaks_the_receipt` (D4's second case: one same-length byte change under
#         the unchanged receipt fails naming the line, the artifact is otherwise container-clean, and a
#         receipt recomputed for the mutated bytes is green again),
#         `test_the_receipt_compares_the_lines_own_bytes` (the anchors are bytes, not a reader's value:
#         a CRLF rewrite the container rules read as whitespace is refused by the receipt),
#         `test_the_byte_layer_ends_the_reading` (a byte-layer violation is `oracle.utf8` alone),
#         `test_the_line_rule_is_the_whole_lines_own` (an unterminated last record is
#         `oracle.whole-lines` alone; a blank line is no JSON object),
#         `test_the_validate_mode_reports_a_verdict` (PASS/FAIL/INCOMPLETE with exit 0/1/2),
#         `test_an_unreadable_input_is_incomplete_never_a_pass` (a missing artifact, a receipt that is
#         not JSON, and a receipt document writing a member name twice all exit 2),
#         `test_disable_rule_turns_exactly_one_rule_off` (the flag reaches the shipped reading),
#         `test_the_validator_reads_no_file` (the validator's input is the bytes: every file-opening
#         name refused, it still answers — D2's "source absent from the process"),
#         `test_a_container_of_json_objects_that_is_no_agents_session_passes` and
#         `test_the_registry_holds_no_foreign_format_vocabulary` (D2's negative space: the rules judge
#         the container, and the frozen surface names no foreign format's vocabulary) — and
#         `test_the_corpus_arms_run_the_shipped_command_not_the_python_validator` (the arms are the
#         command's own).
#   oracle.receipt-integrity — no Go test reads the frozen oracle artifact or its receipt: the case a
#         row once cited here (`TestFixturesMatchTheirGenerator`) hashes the Go fixture and growth trees
#         (`ccc/internal/ccc/fixtures_test.go`), never `scripts/tests/testdata/codex-oracle/`, so
#         nothing it does can move when the artifact, its receipt or their comparison changes. D4's
#         discharge is the required `selftest` step itself — the surface that reads those files: the
#         receipt cases named under `oracle.utf8, oracle.whole-lines` above (D4's verify case and its
#         second case, and the anchors-are-bytes case), plus
#         `test_a_line_feed_moved_is_named_by_the_line_whose_bytes_diverged` (a moved delimiter byte
#         changes the anchor count and the shared anchors are still compared, so the line it diverged
#         on is named), beside the `oracle.receipt-integrity` mutations of `--selftest-mutations`
#         (7 pairs: a changed byte under the unchanged receipt, another whole-file digest, a wrong byte
#         count, no lines, one line fewer, another line's anchor, and a receipt that is not an object),
#         and the combined pair under `oracle.utf8` (`a byte that is not UTF-8 under the unchanged
#         receipt`: a same-length byte masked under the frozen receipt cites `oracle.receipt-integrity`
#         beside its own rule and still cites exactly it with `oracle.utf8` disabled — the receipt's
#         comparison is over raw bytes, independent of the text layer).
#   D3 — the Codex judgment is the binary's: the native check's own unflagged run is a native harness
#         run, not a gate step; its verdicts (and the disclosure arm, where the harness refuses the
#         artifact the offline rules accept) are quoted in §3 of docs/evidence/0009a-native-oracle-v2.md.
#   D5 — the deletions are declared: §2 of the same record carries the deleted rule list with each
#         rule's fixture and mutations, derived from PR #19's diff; the gate cannot hold a deleted rule.

column4: 0009a-native-oracle-v2.md §2-§3 (the writer's own bytes: each written line decodes as exactly one JSON object — the case's `decodeRollout` fails a line that is not one — the framing clause the rule states; the member-name-uniqueness and unpaired-surrogate clauses have no Go producer and are the corpus mutations `a line holding a member name twice` and `a line holding an unpaired surrogate escape`; the integer-reading clause — a line's integers are read by their digits and never converted, so the interpreter's digit limit decides no verdict — has no Go producer either and is pinned by the selftest step's `test_a_line_holding_a_big_integer_is_one_json_object_whatever_the_limit`)
